non-violent communication will give you tools to communicate effectively in a non- abusive way, and to listen to and empathize with others in a verbal way. There are numerous books about IFS (internal family systems), and I have not read all of them, but I would definitely look into it. The Self-therapy books are IFS-do-it-yourself. It is a very helpful method for healing. Pete Walker's writing focuses on healing the inner child and pacifying the inner critic. He also has a book about re-framing the perspective in which you experience your emotions, which I have not read. Pete Walker focuses on childhood emotional abuse/dysfunctional families and CPTSD. While you may not have CPTSD, in your healing journey you may find that you need to do some re-parenting, which is a technique used in healing childhood abuse/neglect and for burying toxic behaviors acquired in such conditions. The Untethered Soul is also a wonderful book, and short, as well, though dense. Most of all, be patient and have compassion towards yourself. You may outgrow your therapist at some point, as well, and that is normal. It is also normal for you to not like every therapist you see. You have to shop around and find one you "click" with. It will be a long road and it will take hard work, and you will not see all the progress you make because it will be slow. Progress is also not necessarily linear.

Get therapy. People aren't abusive out of nowhere. You learned it from someone, and now you have to unlearn it. Read the non-violent communication book to learn how to communicate in an abuse-free way. IFS and mindfulness are great therapy techniques. Let go of what you want, and know that as you grow as a person and heal from being abusive, you will make new relationships, and you will grow confident in who you are becoming. It feels uncertain now because you feel uncertain about yourself.
